title: The Infinite Library
evidence_boundary: The infinite library, library cards, shelves, librarians, windows, and books are metaphors for situated perspective, selective attention, inherited framing, and belief revision. The script does not claim the mind is literally a library or that every interpretation is equally accurate.
desired_movement: From hearing a perspective as a truth claim to treating it as one situated volume that can be opened, tested, compared, borrowed from, or returned.
grounding: The library metaphor lands in an ordinary room with a hand, screen, chair, and breath.
invitation: When the next idea feels like truth, would you check which shelf it came from—and what the neighboring books say?
end_card_question: Which shelf did this idea come from—and what do the neighboring books say?
voice_standard: Liam — warm, sly, brilliant, and intimate; a friend leveling with the viewer at midnight. Dry on the library jokes, lucid through the mechanism, tender at the turn, grounded near the end, and nearly a whisper on the final question.

motif_visual_echo.treatment: Scene 9 turns neglected library doors into openings; narration preserves the library metaphor and does not reuse a prior line verbatim.
